answer: The cheapest real defence: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because mesa only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, violet is enforced in the ledger: Detection is retrospective: payouts for a flagged cluster are clawed back after the fact. Any dune approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
